title: 'Day 6: Rotate butane and inspect its torsional profile'
---

A **5–10 minute exploration**, using a prediction before each control change. The diagram and result update locally; no network service is used.

## Predict first

Along C2 → C3, predict the terminal methyl-group dihedral for anti and gauche butane. Are both staggered?

## Explore

1. Use the anti preset and identify the front dot, rear circle and both CH₃ groups. Trace the connected C1–C2–C3–C4 framework.

2. Move to gauche and then to the second gauche arrangement near 300°. Follow only the rear substituent set and explain which connectivity stays fixed.

3. Inspect the eclipsed preset and sweep through a full turn. Match the diagram to the marker on the qualitative energy profile; distinguish methyl/methyl eclipsing from methyl/H eclipsing.

## Take-away

Explain why a different Newman projection can still be the same molecule. Why must this qualitative energy plot not be used directly to calculate an equilibrium population?

## Model and limits

The projection has a fixed C2 → C3 viewing direction. Blue bonds begin on the front carbon; dark bonds on the rear carbon. The curve is a smooth illustrative interpolation through canonical butane arrangements in arbitrary units, not measured free energies or a model of rotation rate.
